title: Types can overlap

blocks.heading: Types can overlap
blocks.text: Government types describe different features such as head of state, accountability and concentration of power. A republic can be democratic or authoritarian; a constitutional monarchy may coexist with parliamentary democracy. Do not treat the labels as mutually exclusive.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Monarchy
blocks.text: A monarchy has a monarch as head of state, commonly through hereditary succession. The monarch’s powers vary; the title alone does not establish absolute control.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Parliamentary democracy
blocks.text: Parliamentary democracy bases democratic government on an elected parliament to which the executive is accountable. Voting, scrutiny and rights need effective practice; the name alone does not establish equal influence.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Republic
blocks.text: A republic has a non-hereditary public office as head of state rather than a monarch. This does not by itself establish free elections or limits on executive power.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: One-party state
blocks.text: A one-party state permits political rule through a single authorised party without genuine competitive party alternation. Restricted competition limits voters’ alternatives; compare actual accountability and participation.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Dictatorship
blocks.text: A dictatorship concentrates political power with weak or absent effective democratic checks and competition. It differs from authority exercised within accountable limits; announced efficiency does not establish development benefit.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Totalitarianism
blocks.text: Totalitarianism seeks pervasive control over political and wider social life, often through a dominant ideology and coercive institutions. It describes an extent of control beyond the mere presence of a strong executive; avoid inferring it from one policy.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Apply the distinction
blocks.text: Differentiate a monarchy from a republic on the head-of-state dimension. A monarchy has a monarch, commonly hereditary; a republic has a non-hereditary public head-of-state office. Neither label alone establishes democracy.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
